scenarios.prompt: change.json says componentMode=existing. specs/spec.md is baseline-ready, but specs/design.md is missing. The user asks the agent to write the AR requirements now.
expected: reads and validates both canonical paths before specifying an existing component
blocks the change because the design baseline is missing and routes baseline creation to devflow-init
does not infer missing design facts or proceed with an incomplete baseline

scenarios.prompt: A genuinely new component has componentMode=new and neither canonical document exists. Create the specification artifacts for its first AR.
expected: accepts EMPTY as the spec and design baseline without invoking devflow-init
creates srs.md, delta-spec.md, tasks.md skeleton, traceability.md, and change.json under specs/changes/ARXXX-topic
makes the purpose change and ADDED requirement blocks complete enough to construct the first component spec with scenarios from an empty baseline

scenarios.prompt: change.json says componentMode=new, but baseline-ready specs/spec.md and specs/design.md already exist for the same component.
expected: treats the mode and repository mismatch as blocking
asks for an explicit mode correction instead of silently treating the component as new or existing
does not overwrite either canonical document

scenarios.prompt: IFR-002 changes only the invalid-input error in SPEC-IF-003 from ERR_UNSUPPORTED to ERR_INVALID_ARG. The section also defines timeout, concurrency, and success side effects that are unchanged.
expected: places a MODIFIED operation under the MODIFIED requirements section with a stable operation ID, target section ID, and selector limited to invalid-input error semantics
records the base excerpt, resulting local content, regression semantics, and an explicit preservation clause
does not replace the whole section or drop timeout, concurrency, success, or other unmentioned behavior

scenarios.prompt: The AR renames the display title of SPEC-FR-004 but does not change its behavior.
expected: uses a RENAMED operation with from and to names
keeps SPEC-FR-004 as the stable identity
states that body, acceptance, and behavioral semantics are preserved

scenarios.prompt: delta-spec.md was based on revision abc. Before R1, the same target field in specs/spec.md changed at revision def.
expected: detects an overlapping change using recorded base revision or digest
stops and requests semantic conflict resolution instead of applying the older patch
keeps change.json.baseRevision immutable and records the resolution in delta provenance and gate evidence

scenarios.prompt: The agent initialized traceability with only columns labeled 需求条目, Code, and Test and wants R1 to proceed.
expected: rejects the incomplete matrix
uses the fixed chain 需求条目 to Spec Section to Design Section/Case to Task to Code/Test to Evidence
fills the first two columns now and marks downstream cells with stage-specific TBD values

scenarios.prompt: Specification content is ready. The agent puts R1/R2/R3 gate rows into tasks.md and marks R1 passed itself.
expected: keeps tasks.md as a task and TDD evidence skeleton without lifecycle gate state
stores gates only in change.json and sets R1 to pending for independent review
does not let the specification author mark R1 passed

scenarios.prompt: The request says the operation should be fast and memory efficient but provides no environment or threshold.
expected: does not invent a number or write a non-testable NFR
asks the source owner for QAS environment and response measures or records a blocking open question
keeps change.json gates.r1 blocked while the requirement fact is unresolved

scenarios.prompt: The SRS puts FR, IFR, NFR, and CON entries under one generic requirements chapter.
expected: separates FR and IFR into the functional requirements chapter
places NFR entries in a distinct non-functional requirements chapter with QAS and measurable response
places verifiable constraints in their own chapter and updates the SRS self-check
uses FR/IFR/NFR/CON IDs without adding an SRS prefix

scenarios.prompt: FR-001 says administrators can create, query, modify, and delete policies across immediate and scheduled modes, with one shared Acceptance list.
expected: splits independently observable CRUD and timing-mode behaviors into focused requirements
preserves the original source while giving each child its own acceptance
asks for confirmation before moving any child behavior out of the current AR and records its destination

scenarios.prompt: NFR-001 says requests should usually finish within 100 ms, but does not identify the source, event, operating environment, response, percentile, or failure condition.
expected: requires stimulus source, stimulus, environment, response, and response measure
rejects usually and the bare 100 ms value as an incomplete measurable contract
blocks R1 or asks the responsible owner for the missing context and threshold semantics

scenarios.prompt: NFR-001 combines peak-load latency, memory capacity, degraded-mode recovery time, and configuration integrity into one QAS with several environments and thresholds.
expected: splits independent performance, capacity, reliability, and security concerns into separate NFR entries
gives each NFR one coherent environment, response measure, and source without duplicating an acceptance block
does not create empty NFR entries for unrelated quality dimensions

scenarios.prompt: The author adds componentMode, baseRevision, canonical paths, Priority, Impact, Affected Spec Section, Current Behavior, Semantics To Preserve, and an author self-check to every SRS requirement.
expected: keeps identity, mode, base revision, and artifact state only in change.json
keeps impact, canonical target, current behavior, and preservation semantics only in delta-spec.md
keeps SRS focused on problem, scope, desired requirements, sources, constraints, assumptions, and open questions
does not duplicate NFR QAS as a second acceptance block or retain author self-check in the deliverable

scenarios.prompt: The author writes component spec as a collection of delta operations and puts ADDED, MODIFIED, REMOVED, and RENAMED records together in one generic operations chapter.
expected: keeps specs/spec.md as current Purpose plus Requirements and Scenarios without delta markers
separates delta-spec operations into ADDED, MODIFIED, REMOVED, and RENAMED requirement sections
requires complete added requirement blocks, safe partial-or-full modified results, removal reason and migration semantics, and rename from/to while preserving the stable ID
